newsitem.title: USA: Gephardt- tentative strike deal at McDonnell.
newsitem.headline: Gephardt- tentative strike deal at McDonnell.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas Corp reached a tentative agreement Friday with the International Association of Machinists ending a 94-day strike in St. Louis, U.S. House Democratic Leader Richard Gephardt said.

"As a member of the St. Louis community, I am pleased to announce that a tentative agreement has been reached, pending ratification of the membership, to bring an end to the dispute between the machinists union and the McDonnell Douglas Corp," Gephardt told a news conference.
In recent days, negotiations between the company and the union representing over 6,000 striking workers have been conducted in the office of the Missouri congressman.
"This strike has strained our economy and put many of our families at risk," Gephardt said.
The key issue in the strike was job security and the outsourcing of work to companies in other cities.
Gephardt said the deal meant that jobs would remain in St. Louis.
He and negotiators declined to discuss terms of the agreement before they were considered by members for ratification.
Union leaders said the ratification meeting would be held as soon as possible.
Gerry Oulson, president of District 837 of the union, said he hoped a ratification meeting could be arranged by Wednesday or Thursday next week.
Federal Mediation and Concilliation Service Director John Calhoun Wells praised Gephardt's role in convening the talks in his office after negotiations broke down in St. Louis on August 16.
Gephardt "placed the work stoppage in its proper national context," Wells said.
Gephardt said the agreement will benefit the company and the workers. He said it will make the firm more competitive and would jobs in St. Louis.
